propositions: Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 rungs in MODEL_LADDER both declare a 1,000,000 token window, causing escalation from sonnet to opus to gain zero additional context capacity.

A context-limit retry escalating from sonnet to opus fails again at the same window limit but at higher opus pricing, after a second full round-trip, and the failure is silent — operators misdiagnose it as even the largest model could not fit it.

Both declared window figures (haiku 200k, sonnet 1M, opus 1M) are verified correct against the provider's live Models API max_input_tokens, so the defect is in escalation consumption, not in the table.
A new escalation_rungs() function must filter models_at_or_above() to exclude any rung whose declared window is not strictly greater than the last kept rung's, ensuring no paid no-op calls occur.

The filter is applied only to context-limit escalation loops (pass1_with_ladder, run_focused_finder), leaving models_at_or_above, MODEL_LADDER, and largest_window_tokens unchanged to preserve provider stickiness and size budget observables.

Structural guards must assert that MODEL_LADDER windows are non-decreasing across entries and that escalation_rungs returns strictly increasing windows from every start rung, preventing future reintroduction of no-op escalations.
